newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hokkaido Bank says to pay back 70 bln yen in loans.
newsitem.headline: Hokkaido Bank says to pay back 70 bln yen in loans.

text.p: Hokkaido Bank Ltd said on Tuesday it hopes to finish repaying 70 billion yen in subordinated loans from life insurance firms and other financial institutions by the end of this fiscal year next March 31.
As a result, the bank's capital-adequacy ratio would be lower than eight percent, the level required for banks with overseas branches according to rules of the Bank for International Settlements.
In June, the bank closed all of its overseas operations, including its New York branch and offices in London and Hong Kong, a bank spokesman said.
At the end of March 1995, the bank's capital-adequacy ratio stood at 8.7 percent, he said.
